stem: During pharmacist consultation, an out-of-state Ambien prescription is presented 31 days after issue and otherwise appears authentic. What is the Massachusetts consequence?

choices.text: Fill because federal Schedule IV prescriptions remain refillable for six months after documenting whether the Massachusetts 30-day out-of-state initial-fill condition did not also apply.
Use the five-day contiguous-state narcotic rule.
Accept the prescription after telephone verification on day 31.
Do not use the out-of-state Schedule IV pathway because its 30-day issue window has elapsed.
Change the issue date to the date the pharmacy received it.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'Do not use the out-of-state Schedule IV pathway because its 30-day issue window has elapsed.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Fill because federal Schedule IV prescriptions remain refillable for six months.' would require that the Massachusetts 30-day out-of-state initial-fill condition did not also apply. The decisive cue appears in 'During pharmacist consultation, an out-of-state Ambien prescription is presented 31 days after issue and otherwise appears authentic. What is the Massachusetts consequence?'.
